source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 3: integral of g(x) = f(x) + f(4 - x) for a piecewise f; book p. 101. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'.

blocks.prompt: 3 Let \(f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 & \text{if } 0 \leq x \leq 2 \\ 2x + 1 & \text{if } 2 < x \leq 4 \end{cases}\). Here \(g(x)\) is defined as: \(g(x) = f(x) + f(4 - x)\). Compute: \(\int_{0}^{4} g(x)\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
We need the integral of \(f(x) + f(4 - x)\) over \([0, 4]\).
Property IV says \(\int_0^4 f(4 - x)\,dx = \int_0^4 f(x)\,dx\), so the answer is \(2\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx\).
Then split \(\int_0^4 f\) at the corner \(x = 2\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2\) on \([0, 2]\), \(2x + 1\) on \((2, 4]\); \(g(x) = f(x) + f(4 - x)\).
To find: \(\int_{0}^{4} g(x)\,dx\).
Method: Property IX (sum rule), Property IV with \(a = 0\), \(b = 4\), then Property III at \(x = 2\).

Use Property IV
\[\int_{0}^{4} g(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx + \int_{0}^{4} f(4 - x)\,dx\]
\[= 2\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx\]
Why: \(\int_0^b f(b - x)\,dx = \int_0^b f(x)\,dx\); here \(b = 4\).

Split \(\int_0^4 f\) at \(x = 2\)
\[\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{2} x^2\,dx + \int_{2}^{4} (2x + 1)\,dx\]
Why: Property III; the formula of \(f\) changes at 2.

Evaluate the pieces
\[\int_{0}^{2} x^2\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{2} = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
\[\int_{2}^{4} (2x + 1)\,dx = \Big[x^2 + x\Big]_{2}^{4} = 20 - 6 = 14\]
\[\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx = \dfrac{8}{3} + 14 = \dfrac{50}{3}\]
Why: power rule on each piece.

Double it
\[\int_{0}^{4} g(x)\,dx = 2 \cdot \dfrac{50}{3} = \dfrac{100}{3}\]
Why: from the Property IV step.
